title: What is known about 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE0LB_1LA1RF_0LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE0LB_1LA1RF_0LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine runs a base-5 counter written as markers between blocks; Lean proves its regular sweeps for all block lengths, and an exact fast simulator finds no halt in 1016 steps. No tape is known on which it halts, and nothing here shows that the run never reaches one.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Grouped with the 40-machine block counter, by its tapes
claims.text: The table is not a renaming or mirror image of the core 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE?LF_1LA0LB_??--- (all 720 renamings in both orientations, frames.core_frames). Compared with 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_0RE---: the first pass found the same tape at every sweep end up to 1011 steps. An observation, not a proof; the family's Lean theorems do not cover this machine.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 78,449 cells have been visited and 20,717 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.558).

claims.title: The sweeps, for all block lengths
claims.text: Fifteen pieces of a sweep (the leftward wave across a block and across a carried marker, the turns at a marker in each phase, the rightward waves, the overflow at the left end) and nine whole sweeps: one per phase of the last marker, with one and two carries, and overflows with one and two markers.

claims.title: An exact fast simulator
claims.text: The run-length simulator c/rl.c of the family lead (shift rules found and applied automatically, like symtm on concrete numbers) gives the same tape at every sweep end of the first 108 steps as the run without shift rules and as the plain simulator.

claims.title: The counter rules
claims.text: To 10<sup>11</sup> steps, 251,364 of the 251,409 sweeps are regular turns and 15 are overflows, each exactly as the two rules say; the other 30 are merges.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>16</sup> steps
claims.text: The fast simulator runs 10,000,000,062,703,342 steps without a halt; F is entered 182,039,994 times and reads a 0 every time.

claims.title: Merges of separated markers never halt
claims.text: All 48 merges of two markers with at least 12 words of block on either side (each failing turn, each phase of the marker before it, with and without a carried marker after it) run symbolically, for all block lengths, for 12 sweeps or until the carry leaves them: none halts.

claims.title: Same class (same tapes or same markers, not the same run) as 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_0RE---, 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_1LB---, 1RB0LC_0RC0RE_1RD1LF_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_0RB---, 1RB0LC_0RC1RF_1RD0RE_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_1RE---
claims.text: Class I of the five runs of the family. The direct members have the same tape at every sweep end to 10<sup>11</sup> steps. The mirrored members have the same markers at every sweep end from sweep 157,376 on.

claims.title: No halting configuration known
claims.text: None of 2,000 random short tapes of the same shape halts within 20,000 steps, and no merge of separated markers halts. Here F is entered on the detour of every regular E1 step and has read a 0 every time; nothing here shows a tape on which it would read a 1, nor that none is ever reached.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Only if two merges ever meet; a question about the long-run arithmetic of the counter.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LF_1LC0RD_0LD0LC_1RE0LA_0RA0RC_0RE--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_0RC0RE_1RD1LF_1LE0RA_0LA0LE_0RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The machine counts in base 5 with markers that drift along the tape and now and then collide; nothing it has done so far comes close to halting.

facts.text: proved in Lean for all block lengths.
No halt in the C simulator; 78,449 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Next to the forty-machine core
html: The family plan groups this machine with the nested block counter: 40 holdouts that are one five-state core 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE?LF_1LA0LB_??--- in different frames. This machine's table is not a renaming or mirror image of that core, so the family's Lean theorems (the visit rule, its closed form, the conserved residues and drifts) are not proved for it.

What ties it to the family is an observation about runs: compared with 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE1LF_1LA0LB_0RE---, the first pass found the same tape at every sweep end up to 1011 steps. If that held for the whole run the two machines would write the same tapes, but their halting transitions are read in different situations, so even then one halting question would not settle the other without a further argument.

sections.heading: A base-5 counter of markers
html: Stop the machine each time the head steps onto a new cell at the growing end. The tape is then always
long blocks of the word 0010 separated by markers, each in one of six phases: 1 (0), 0 (0′), 0011 (1), 011 (2), 11 (3), 00111 (4).

Between two such moments the head makes one sweep: a wave runs from the end toward the start, passing every marker in phase 4, and turns at the first marker that is not; that marker goes up one phase, and on the way back the phase-4 markers are reset to phase 0. The phases are the digits of a counter in base 5 that counts the sweeps. When every marker is in phase 4 the wave runs to the start of the tape and the counter gains a digit (a new marker at the end).

The blocks around a marker change with its phase (phase 0 takes two words from the block before it, phases 0′ and 3 one), so the markers drift toward the start, the last one fastest. When a marker has used up the block before it, it merges with the marker there: a few special sweeps, after which the counter goes on. Lean proves the regular sweeps for all block lengths.

Run the counter. The tape between two sweeps, written as its first block b0 and the markers with the block after each. Each step is one sweep of the machine by the two regular rules; the run stops at a merge, where a marker has used up the block before it and the machine does something special.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html:
The only halting transition is F1, and F is entered only at some merges (and, in two of the sixteen machines, on a detour that does what the others do in one step). Every entry into F so far has read a 0. Every merge of two markers with long blocks around them runs, symbolically and for all block lengths, without halting. In this machine even random short tapes of the same shape do not halt, so no halting configuration reachable in this shape is known at all.

The counter is deterministic, and the block lengths it makes look very regular (many are close to multiples of powers of 5), but nothing here decides whether such a coincidence ever comes.
Sixteen holdouts run this counter, in five distinct runs; this machine is in class I. The family is described in full on the page of 1RB0LC_0RC0RB_1LD0RE_0LE0LF_1LA0LB_0LC---.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.558).
After 109 steps the tape spans 78,449 cells (53 left of the start, 61,854 right), with a density of 1s of 0.264.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: Marker counter (class I): a base-5 counter of markers between 0010-blocks, whose markers drift and merge; it halts only if its E1 detour through F ever reads a 1. No halt in 10^16 steps.
